title: Drop the oldest record, add flush(), and limit batch bytes

pr.title: shipper: keep the newest records, flush(), byte-limited batches, JSON lines
pr.description:
Four changes to the async sink:

- A full queue now drops its oldest record and counts the drop in the registry, so the newest lines of an incident survive.
- `flush()` waits until the transport has each queued record. The shutdown hook calls it before `close()`.
- A batch holds at most `maxBatchBytes` of text, so the collector never sees a request above its limit.
- `toJsonLine()` encodes a record for the collector.

Tests cover each change.

bugs.note: Lock order across two files: push() calls registry_.countDrop() while it holds the sink mutex, and countDrop() takes the registry mutex. The unchanged SinkRegistry::remove() and ~SinkRegistry() hold the registry mutex and call AsyncSink::detach(), which takes the sink mutex. registry.h states the order (registry before sink), so a push into a full queue during remove() deadlocks both threads.

A predicate loop that checks the wrong condition: flush() waits for queue_.empty(), but the unchanged worker pops a batch before it writes it, so the queue is empty while the last batch is still in flight. flush() returns before the transport has the records; the unchanged close() shows the right predicate, queue_.empty() && writing_ == 0. The shutdown hook then loses the last records.

traps.why: pop_front() on an empty deque is undefined, but the branch runs only when the queue holds capacity records, and the unchanged validate() that the constructor calls refuses a capacity of 0.

A record larger than maxBatchBytes would never fit and leave an empty batch in a busy loop, but the unchanged Record::make() cuts each text at kMaxRecordBytes, and the unchanged validate() keeps maxBatchBytes at or above kMaxRecordBytes.

The encoder escapes only quotes and backslashes, which looks like invalid JSON for control characters, but the unchanged Record::make(), the only way to build a Record, turns each byte below 0x20 into a space and cuts on a UTF-8 boundary.
